Create and monitor a delete button

Source: R/delete.R
delete_button.Rd

These functions are used internally in faketables

Usage

.delete_button(
  rowId,
  ...,
  .delete_style = "background: #bf5959; color: #fff; border: none; width: 100%",
  .delete_label = "Delete"
)

.create_delete_listener(ns = shiny::NS(NULL))

Arguments

rowId

The .rowId value that corresponds to the row where the button will be displayed

...

Further arguments to pass to shiny::column(). This can include width. If not provided, width will default to 2.

.delete_style

The CSS style for the delete button

.delete_label

The label for the delete button

ns

The output of a call to shiny::NS()

Value

A shiny::column() containing a shiny::actionButton() that allows users to send a delete request.

An HTML <head> tag with the button listener

Details

The delete button itself does not actually delete a row from the data, this only creates a button that reports which row a user wishes to delete.

There are three components required to use the buttons. The first is placing .create_delete_listener() somewhere in the shiny app's ui. The second is calling .delete_button() to create the button and then inserting it using shiny::insertUI(). The third is creating a shiny event listener that acts on the button presses by monitoring input$table_btns.

Author

Joe Marlo

Examples

if (interactive()) {
# this example creates a button for every row of `mtcars`
# when the user presses a button, it will print the inputId of the button pressed
shiny::shinyApp(
  ui = shiny::tagList(
    .create_delete_listener(), # add button listener
    shiny::div(id = 'delete-buttons') # create div for buttons to be inserted
  ),
  server = \(input, output, session) {
    mtcars |>
      tibble::rownames_to_column() |>
      dplyr::pull(.data$rowname) |>
      purrr::map_chr(digest::digest) |> # create row ids
      purrr::walk(\(x) {
        shiny::insertUI( # insert delete button into ui
          selector = '#delete-buttons',
          where = 'afterBegin',
          ui = shiny::fluidRow(.delete_button(x, list(width = 2)))
        )
      })

    shiny::observe({
     print(glue::glue('Button {input$table_btns} was pressed'))
    }) |>
     shiny::bindEvent(input$table_btns)
  }
)
}
